M8SkillLoader.description: Loads a skill file (prompt text) and outputs it as a knowledge pack for M8 · LLM Inference.

skill.name: skill
skill.tooltip: Pick an uploaded skill file. Use the Upload button on the node to add one.

enabled.name: enabled
enabled.tooltip: Turn off to output an empty skill, as if unplugging the wire without editing the workflow.

extra_text.name: extra_text
extra_text.tooltip: Extra text appended after this skill. Handy for one-off tweaks you do not want to write into the file.

skill.name: skill
skill.tooltip: The loaded skill, feed it into the skill input of M8 · LLM Inference.

M8LLMInference.description: Calls an external LLM over an OpenAI-compatible API: two prompt boxes, model dropdown, thinking effort. Accepts a skill, images and audio; outputs text.

provider.name: provider
provider.tooltip: Pick a provider. Changing it fills in that provider's default base_url and thinking options. For anything else choose Custom and enter the address yourself.

base_url.name: base_url
base_url.tooltip: API address. Defaults to https://api.deepseek.com/v1; point it at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

api_key.name: api_key
api_key.tooltip: Leave empty to use the key stored on the server (recommended: Save key keeps it out of the workflow file). Anything typed here applies to this node only and is written into the workflow.

model.name: model
model.tooltip: Fill in the address and key, then click Refresh models. You can also type a model name directly.

system_prompt.name: system_prompt
system_prompt.tooltip: System prompt: persona, tone, output format. Leave empty to send only the user prompt.

user_prompt.name: user_prompt
user_prompt.tooltip: What you want to ask. Can be wired from another node's text output.

thinking.name: thinking
thinking.tooltip: Thinking effort. Off sends no extra request; higher asks the model to think more. If the provider rejects the parameter it is dropped and the request retried.

show_thinking.name: show_thinking
show_thinking.tooltip: Show the model's thinking on the node panel (default off: it is usually long). Display only, the text output is unaffected.

temperature.name: temperature
temperature.tooltip: Randomness. Lower for steady work like prompt writing, higher for creative ones.

max_tokens.name: max_tokens
max_tokens.tooltip: Upper bound on the reply length. It is a cap, not a target.

timeout.name: timeout
timeout.tooltip: Request timeout in seconds. For slow thinking models give it 300 or more.

skill.name: skill
skill.tooltip: Wire this from M8 · Skill Loader. Its content is appended after the system prompt as reference material.

skill_auto.name: skill_auto
skill_auto.tooltip: Inject every uploaded skill and let the model decide which applies. Off by default: once the library grows, each turn carries a few irrelevant ones and burns tokens.

image.name: image
image.tooltip: Feed images to a vision model. Multiple images are sent together.

audio.name: audio
audio.tooltip: Feed audio to a model that accepts it (converted to WAV).

extra_params.name: extra_params
extra_params.tooltip: Extra request parameters as a JSON object, merged into the request body.

M8LLMLocal.description: Runs inference on a local GGUF model: no network, no API key. Models live in ComfyUI's models/LLM folder. Pair it with an mmproj file in the same folder to enable vision; a skill node can supply a knowledge pack.

model.name: model
model.tooltip: The main .gguf in models/LLM. If the list is empty, check that folder.

system_prompt.name: system_prompt
system_prompt.tooltip: System prompt. Combined with any skill into the system block, skill first.

user_prompt.name: user_prompt
user_prompt.tooltip: What you want to ask this round.

extra_text.name: extra_text
extra_text.tooltip: Extra text appended after the prompt. Good for additional requirements, style constraints, fields to reference.

image.name: image
image.tooltip: Images for the model to look at. Without it the run is text only. Needs an mmproj file next to the model.

skill.name: skill
skill.tooltip: Wire the output of a skill loader node here to use it as a knowledge pack.

mmproj.name: mmproj
mmproj.tooltip: Multimodal projection file. Auto-paired by name; pick one manually if that guessed wrong.

ctx.name: ctx
ctx.tooltip: Context length. Larger uses more memory; only needed for long conversations or many images.

gpu_layers.name: gpu_layers
gpu_layers.tooltip: -1 = offload as many layers as the GPU allows. 0 = CPU only.

thinking.name: thinking
thinking.tooltip: Whether the model should show its thinking. Off gives cleaner output.

status.name: status
status.tooltip: How this run went: token count, vision or text, cache hit or fresh load.

M8CameraControl.description: Visual camera positioning: outputs the matching camera prompt (direction split by ratio + height / distance / tilt + lens / depth / motion / composition / style).

pos_x.name: pos_x
pos_x.tooltip: Left / Right (X): -1 is fully left, +1 fully right.

pos_y.name: pos_y
pos_y.tooltip: Up / Down (Y): -1 is looking up from below, +1 from above.

pos_z.name: pos_z
pos_z.tooltip: Near / Far (Z): -1 is close, +1 is distant.

roll.name: roll
roll.tooltip: Roll: tilts the horizon (dutch angle) once past the dead zone.

config.name: config
config.tooltip: Advanced JSON: weight budgets, per-step output, lens / depth / motion / composition / style switches.

prompt.name: prompt
prompt.tooltip: The camera prompt, ready to go into a positive prompt.

M8MultiCharacter.description: Edit several characters' prompts and on-canvas regions, assembled into one ready-to-use prompt.

format.name: format
format.tooltip: attn = Attention Couple, regional = Regional Prompts, plain = comma-separated text with no region syntax.

use_fill.name: use_fill
use_fill.tooltip: Fill the areas no character covers with the base prompt.

config.name: config
config.tooltip: The character list as JSON: name, prompt, region (x/y/w/h), blend weight, feather, enabled.

base_prompt.name: base_prompt
base_prompt.tooltip: Base prompt, merged with the global prompt.

width.name: width
width.tooltip: Canvas width the regions are laid out on.

height.name: height
height.tooltip: Canvas height the regions are laid out on.

prompt.name: prompt
prompt.tooltip: The assembled prompt, ready for a positive prompt.

M8Whale.presetRunPrompt:
Run one image on this canvas. Please work like this:
1. Look at the canvas structure first and find where the prompt goes (keyword or positive-prompt nodes).
2. Write a prompt yourself and fill it in; the subject and style are up to you.
3. Queue it once it is filled in.
4. Tell me what prompt you wrote and which node you put it in.

If this canvas cannot be run directly (missing models, no prompt node, structure unclear),
explain what is missing first. Do not change my parameters on your own.
M8Whale.presetLoraPrompt:
Help me pick a few LoRAs. Call list_loras first to see what I have installed,
then recommend 3 to 5 that fit what this canvas is currently doing:
what each one does and why it suits this scene.
If the canvas has a node that takes a LoRA, ask whether I want it filled in - do not change it directly.
M8Whale.presetErrorsPrompt:
Check whether any recent task failed. Call get_recent_errors to get the records.
If something failed, say clearly: which node, what the message was, the likely cause, and how to fix it.
If nothing failed, just say so. Do not make one up for me.

web.loraLede: Drop in a .safetensors file and read back its training parameters and training tags.
web.loraPrivacyLead: The file is never uploaded and never written to disk.
web.loraPrivacyBody: Parsing reads only the beginning of the file (usually a few KB to a few tens of KB) and drops the reference afterwards - even a several-hundred-MB model takes an instant, because not a single byte of tensor data is read.
web.loraDrop: Click to choose, drag it in, or paste with Ctrl+V
web.metaLede: Drop in an image and it is parsed automatically: generation parameters, embedded workflow, EXIF, file info. Everything is read on this machine and the image is never uploaded.

web.promptsLede: One card per concept prompt - framing, lighting, texture, art style and the like. Write it, file it under a category, copy it in one click when you need it. Everything is kept on this machine and is still here next time.
web.pgEmptyBody: Click "New card" in the top right - name it something like "low-angle framing", write the prompt as from below, low angle..., then pick a category.
web.pgNamePlaceholder: For example: framing / lighting / texture / art style
web.pixelLede: Compress an image into low-resolution pixel art: antialiasing convolution, area-average downsampling, sharpening convolution, colour-reduction dithering, nearest-neighbour upscale. Everything is computed on this machine and the image is never uploaded.
web.pixelNoteLead: The upscale uses nearest-neighbour, not interpolation.
web.pixelNoteBody: Interpolation blurs the boundary between pixels, which gives you a low-resolution image rather than pixel art. "Pixel block size" is how many source pixels each pixel covers - larger means coarser grain.
web.pixelDither: Ordered dithering (a regular dot pattern buys smoother transitions)
web.obfLede: Three modes: Tomato cycles pixels along a curve, scramble shuffles in keyed blocks, and nest hides another image in the low bits. All three are reversible and computed on this machine; the image is never uploaded.
web.obfNoteLead: Always save an obfuscated image as PNG.
web.obfNoteMid: Do not crop or resize it either
web.obfNoteBody: - all three modes need the original dimensions to reverse. Scramble is a pure pixel permutation, and nest puts its payload in the least significant bit of every pixel: once the file becomes a JPEG, those low bits are thrown away and nobody can undo it.
web.obfKeyPlaceholder: Any few characters; reversing needs exactly the same ones
web.obfPixels: Also shuffle pixels within each block; messier
web.obfKeyWarn: With no key filled in, anyone who has the image can reverse it.
web.obfTomatoNote: Tomato takes no key and has no other parameters - the shift amount is fixed. This is carried over from the original algorithm on purpose: an image obfuscated there can be reversed here, and one obfuscated here can be reversed there.
web.obfHint2: Scaled automatically to fit the capacity

web.importBodySub: Merge: entries with the same name are skipped, the rest come in as new ones, and nothing already here is touched. Replace: everything here is cleared out first, then these {n} entries are written in.

web.cutNoExportable: Every piece is muted, so there is nothing to export.
web.cutTooSmall: Every piece is too small to cut anything usable.
web.cutPreviewNote: {n} images - muted pieces never show up here
web.cutPreviewReady: All done. Download them one by one, or export the lot.

web.maskInfo: {n} bands - {one} each - about {pct}% covered in total

web.gridSkipped: {n} images were not added: either they are not images, or the limit of {max} is already reached.
web.gridThumbOver: (outside the grid, so it will not be in the collage)
web.gridPreviewReady: Built. Export it once it looks right.
web.paintAdded: Added. Edit it on the right, or drag it on the image to move it.
web.paintNoUndo: There is no stroke left to undo.
web.paintNothing: Nothing written and nothing drawn, so there is nothing to generate.
web.paintPreviewAlt: Preview of the text and brush layers
web.paintStatusHint: In text mode, click to add a box; switch to brush mode and hold to draw.
web.obfCoverTooSmall: The cover image is too small to hold even one secret pixel
web.obfNoRoom: It does not fit: the capacity calculation is off
web.obfImageTooSmall: This image is too small to hold anything
web.obfBadSignature: Signature mismatch: the key is wrong, or there was nothing hidden in this image
web.obfBadHeaderSize: The size recorded in the header is not valid
web.obfHeaderOverflow: The size declared in the header exceeds this image's capacity
web.notAnImage: This file does not contain readable image data
web.obfDropLabelCover: Cover image (the one on the front)
web.obfDropLabelHidden: Image with something hidden in it
web.obfDropHintReverse: Drop the image you want to reverse
web.obfHint2Sized: {w} × {h} - scaled automatically to fit the capacity
web.obfReady: The image is in place - ready when you are.
web.obfTomatoSave: Save it as PNG. Reversing it needs neither a key nor any parameters - bring the image back and hit Reverse.
web.obfAlgoGilbertShift: Cyclic shift along the Gilbert curve
web.obfKeyNone: None - this mode never had one
web.obfCompatBody: This mode is carried over from the original Tomato algorithm with not a single parameter changed. So an image obfuscated there can be reversed here, and one obfuscated here can be reversed there.
web.obfTomatoKeepSize: The dimensions have to stay exactly as they are: reversing derives the shift from the pixel count, so cropping or resizing breaks it.
web.obfTomatoUnlockNote: No key needed. The dimensions have to match the ones used when obfuscating - pass the original image, do not crop or resize it.
web.obfAlgoGilbertUnshift: Reverse shift along the Gilbert curve
web.obfScrambleSave: Save it as PNG. To reverse it you need the same key and the same block size, then paste this key string back in.
web.obfKeyEmptyReversible: Not set - anyone who has it can reverse it
web.obfKeyEmptyExtractable: Not set - anyone who has it can extract the secret
web.obfTicketBody: This string packs the dimensions, block size and fingerprint. Paste it in when reversing and you do not have to remember what you picked. It does not contain the key itself, so you can keep it apart from the key you reverse with.
web.obfTicketWrongMode: This key string was produced by Nest mode, but Scramble is selected.
web.obfTicketSizeMismatch: The key string records {w} × {h}, but this image is {iw} × {ih} - did you pass the wrong image?
web.obfFingerprintMismatch: Fingerprint mismatch: this key string does not belong to this image, so the result will most likely still be garbage.
web.obfNoTicketNote: No key string pasted, so the block size filled in above is used - it has to match the one used when obfuscating.
web.obfNestNeedsTwo: Nesting needs two images: a cover, plus a secret image to hide inside it.
web.obfNestScaled: The secret image was {sw} × {sh} and was scaled down to {dw} × {dh} to fit the capacity - that is the size you get back. For the original size, use a larger cover image.
web.obfNestExact: The secret image went in as it was; what you get back matches it pixel for pixel.
web.obfNestHowTo: Switch to Nest / Reverse, drop the image above in and fill in the same key to get the secret image back. This image looks exactly like the cover - only the lowest bit of every pixel was touched, which the eye cannot pick out.
web.obfSecretSizeNote: The size is the one it had when it was hidden; if the secret image was larger than the capacity, this is the scaled-down size.

web.pgNothingToExport: There is nothing here to export yet.
web.pgReplaced: Replace done: {cards} cards and {groups} categories now.
web.pgImported: Import done: {cards} new cards, {groups} categories, {skipped} skipped as duplicates of what is already here.
web.pgNoStorage: This browser will not store anything (private mode?), so what you add now is gone once you close the page.
web.pgNoPersist: The browser did not grant persistent storage: the data here can be cleared when the disk runs low, so export a backup now and then.
web.pgCardNamePlaceholder: Name this card, for example "low-angle framing"
web.pgDelCardBody: "{name}" holds {n} characters of prompt, and once it is deleted it is gone.
web.pgDelGroupBody: "{name}" holds {n} cards right now. Deleting the category turns those cards into uncategorised ones - they are not deleted with it.
web.pgWrongBackup: This backup is for "{other}", not for the prompt collection.
